title: What a green-card count counts
text: People who became lawful permanent residents in the fiscal year (got a green card), counted when DHS grants the status: either on arrival from abroad with an immigrant visa or by adjusting status inside the U.S. Not the number of immigrant visas the State Department issues, and not entries.
quote: This report reflects admissions at a port of entry rather than the number of visas that the Department of State issues.

title: What a naturalization count counts
text: People aged 18 and over who became U.S. citizens through a naturalization application (Form N-400) in the fiscal year. Children who become citizens through a parent are not counted.
quote: are limited to applicants aged 18 and older and do not represent a complete count of persons who obtained citizenship status in each reporting year.

title: Naturalizations follow processing
text: Yearly naturalizations reflect how many applications USCIS processed, not only how many people applied or wanted to.
quote: Numbers reflect changes in received and processed naturalization applications, which may be affected by limited resources for application processing or pending applications from prior years.

title: Totals only before FY1999
text: Before FY1999 the series has the yearly total only (Yearbook Table 1); classes, new arrivals vs. adjustments and countries start in FY1999. The FY1989–FY1991 peak (1.09, 1.54 and 1.83 million) therefore cannot be broken down here.

title: Rounded to the nearest ten
text: OHSS now rounds published table cells to the nearest ten, so parts may not add exactly to totals. Rounded here: green-card totals FY1977–FY1998 and everything FY2015–FY2024 (FY2024 Yearbook), every naturalization total FY1977–FY2024 (FY2024 Yearbook), and FY2025 (quarterly report). Green-card detail FY1999–FY2014 comes from earlier editions that printed exact counts.
quote: To protect privacy, we round numbers in table cells in all public reports to the nearest ten.

title: Country of birth, and country of nationality for the newest year
text: By-country counts come from the Yearbook by country of birth. The newest year, which only the quarterly report covers, is by country of nationality instead. The two answer different questions (someone born in Hong Kong or the former Soviet Union has another nationality; many Canadian nationals were born elsewhere), so the newest year's ranking is not comparable country by country with earlier years.
quote: PERSONS OBTAINING LAWFUL PERMANENT RESIDENT STATUS BY TYPE OF ADMISSION AND REGION AND COUNTRY OF NATIONALITY: FISCAL YEAR 2025

title: Guadeloupe, Martinique and French Guiana
text: The FY2008 Yearbook (used for FY1999–FY2007) prints Guadeloupe, Martinique and French Guiana as their own rows; later editions count them under France (FY2008 LPRs: France 4,872 + Guadeloupe 33 + Martinique 24 + French Guiana 6 = 4,935 in the FY2017 edition). France's FY1999–FY2007 numbers are therefore slightly lower on a narrower definition.

title: Korea before FY2009
text: The FY2008 Yearbook prints a single Korea row ('Includes both North and South Korea'); the FY2017 Yearbook prints the same FY2008 number as South Korea, footnoted. FY1999–FY2008 are filed under South Korea here.
quote: Data for South Korea prior to Fiscal Year 2009 include a small number of cases from North Korea.

title: Classes of admission
text: The category under which a person became a permanent resident. This series keeps OHSS's six major classes as printed (immediate relatives of U.S. citizens, family-sponsored preferences, employment-based preferences, diversity, refugees, asylees) and groups every smaller class as other. Refugees and asylees count here in the year they adjust to permanent residence, not the year they arrived.
quote: Class of admission refers to category of admission to LPR status rather than admission to the United States.

title: What 'other' contains changes by edition
text: Other is every printed class outside the six major ones, and the printed list changes: FY1999–FY2007 (FY2008 Yearbook) prints parolees, children born abroad to alien residents, NACARA, cancellation of removal, HRIFA and 'Other'. From FY2008 the later editions print Iraqi and Afghan special immigrants, victims of human trafficking and victims of crimes (both 'not available' for FY2008) as rows, and fold NACARA and HRIFA into 'Other'. The six major classes are comparable across the break, except FY2008's special immigrants (see the restatement note).

title: New arrivals and adjustments of status
text: OHSS splits each year's new permanent residents by type of admission: new arrivals, who become permanent residents as they enter the U.S., and adjustments of status, people already in the U.S. (for example on a temporary visa, as refugees or asylees) who change to permanent residence.
quote: type of admission distinguishes new arrivals (who receive admission to the United States at the same time as admission to LPR status) and adjustments of status (who are already within the United States).

title: Withheld small counts
text: The older editions withhold some small cells ("D") to limit disclosure. Where a country's count is withheld, the remainder of the printed total is kept as a 'withheld' row so the year still adds up; FY1999's parolees and HRIFA counts are withheld, so that year's other class is the printed total minus the six major classes.
quote: D Data withheld to limit disclosure.

title: FY2008 special immigrants reclassified
text: The FY2017 Yearbook counts 1,770 fewer FY2008 employment-based 'special immigrants' than the FY2008 Yearbook (7,754 vs. 9,524) and 1,770 more in classes grouped here as other, including 223 Iraqi and Afghan special immigrants. The total is unchanged. The newer edition is used.
quote: Certain Iraqis and Afghans employed by U.S. Government and their spouses and children | 223

title: New arrivals vs. adjustments revised for FY2013–FY2019
text: From the FY2020 Yearbook on, OHSS shows more adjustments of status and fewer new arrivals for FY2013–FY2019 than earlier editions did, with each year's total unchanged (FY2015: 546,000 adjustments in the FY2024 edition vs. 542,315 in the FY2017 edition). OHSS's notes do not explain it. This series uses the newest editions for those years, so FY2013 on are on the revised basis; FY1999–FY2012 come from editions the revision did not touch (FY2011–FY2012 are identical before and after).

title: COVID-19 years (green cards)
text: OHSS reports that new permanent residents fell to a 17-year low in FY2020 and that FY2020–FY2021 had fewer family-sponsored immigrants because of embassy closures.
quote: LPR admissions fell for 3 consecutive years even before the global pandemic contributed to admissions falling further to a 17-year low in 2020.

title: COVID-19 year (naturalizations)
text: USCIS suspended in-person services in 2020; OHSS reports naturalizations fell from 843,590 in FY2019 to 628,250 in FY2020.
quote: naturalizations, which dropped from 843,590 in 2019 to 628,250 in 2020.

title: FY2025 is preliminary
text: FY2025 comes from the quarterly Legal Immigration and Adjustment of Status Report, the only OHSS source for it until the FY2025 Yearbook. Quarterly figures are revised later: the FY2024 report's 1,356,760 new permanent residents became 1,364,090 in the Yearbook.
quote: Information about legal migration flows and adjustments of status provided in this quarterly report is preliminary and based on data available one month after the reporting period.
